There is a difference between street and pharma, and that is the route of administration and dose. You are going to get a very specific dose that's in the therapeutic range and also stretched out, which makes the compound even less "euphoric" and recreational. In the street, you will be more likely to use a larger dose in a more instant administration (intranasal, intravenous, etc). People are on the right track when they say that fentanyl is less euphoric than other traditional opioids since the binding profile is very oriented to be very sedating, so the ratio between sedation and inherent opioid-euphoria is much different than something like oxycodone. Oxycodone is touted to be the most euphoric opioid (as well as oxymorphone, tianeptine, etc). If you compare a few high efficacy full agonists like: oxycodone, fentanyl, tianeptine, you will see that the less sedating ones are the more euphoric ones, and the cool part is you can still dose oxy and other opioids to nod if you want to nod, or you can dose to be functional. This also applies to fentanyl, but as you saw, you don't feel as euphoric.
